subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What side-effect boundary should OpenClaw guarantee for cron and skills dry-run/testing, and should that boundary share a request-scoped contract with global agent dry-run?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementation would define a user-trusted security boundary and new public CLI/Gateway/config semantics across cron, skills, tools, hooks, channels, and external APIs.

options.title: Design one request-scoped contract
options.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool interception semantics together so preview modes make the same no-side-effect guarantees.

options.title: Ship a narrow cron validator first
options.body: Add only cron config, schedule, and delivery validation while leaving skill testing and tool interception to separate follow-up decisions.

options.title: Defer broad dry-run semantics
options.body: Keep command-specific dry-run surfaces only until a maintainer sponsors the shared preview boundary.

recommendation.title: Design one request-scoped contract
recommendation.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool interception semantics together so preview modes make the same no-side-effect guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combined signal from prior issue review plus feature history across cron CLI, skills CLI, and adjacent testing surfaces.
